structured_output.world_model: Time is spent in three places: (epochs) × (cost per epoch) + fixed per-trial cost. Cost per epoch comes from FLOPs plus launch/Python overhead, and under the 4-CPU pin the overhead matters more. Fixed cost covers moving data to the GPU, whitening, and any compile or autotune that leaks into timed code. The current best is the API demo (1.2% accuracy, 0.14 s), so no feasible recipe exists yet. Getting one is the first goal, and it will come from the airbench96 port. In eager mode I expect that port to cost about 1.0–1.3 s per epoch on an A100. At 9 epochs that is roughly 10–12 s including prepare. Without TTA, I expect the port to land about 1–3 pp short of 0.753 at 9 epochs. That would make the accuracy margin binding, so epochs will probably need to go up (10–12), not down. Compile should cut about 15–25% of cost per epoch, and that is the cleanest systems win. Ideas that cut FLOPs (progressive resizing, Muon with a large batch, proxy selection) give back accuracy, and buying it back with extra epochs costs about 10% per epoch. Ideas I002–I008 are forecast as if each were applied to the port, because they cannot be applied to the demo.

forecasts.reason: Without TTA, 9 epochs probably falls 1–3 pp short of 0.753, and an eager port without compile probably takes more than 9.5 s.
The 9→10 branch is the likely one. It costs about 10% more time for roughly 0.5–0.8 pp, which falls outside the 8.5→9 window the hypothesis specifies.
Compile plus fused SGD should remove about 15–25% of cost per epoch. The math is unchanged, so accuracy should be unchanged.
An EMA updated every 5 steps is cheap, but a gain of about 0.2–0.4 pp is within 3-seed noise.
Run-to-run time drift on a dedicated A100 should stay under 2%, and per-seed std should be about 0.2–0.35 pp.
Dropping 1 of 49 batches per epoch saves only about 2% compute, so the 0.3 s claimed saving depends on whether recompiles were actually leaking into timed code.
Newton-Schulz adds cost per step, and batch 2000 halves the number of steps. A first try without tuning is unlikely to save 10% of epochs.
Low-resolution epochs save roughly 15–20% of FLOPs, but on CIFAR-100 at a short epoch budget they probably cost more than 0.2 pp of accuracy.

cruxes: Without TTA, what 3-seed accuracy does the eager airbench96 port actually reach at 9 epochs? Whether it lands above 0.753 or 1–3 pp below decides whether epochs go up or down.
How long does one eager epoch of the port take on this A100 under the 4-CPU pin, and how much of that is launch overhead that compile or CUDA graphs could remove?
How much time do prepare (data transfer and whitening) and any compile or autotune that leaks out of build add per trial, compared with the cost of the epochs themselves?
